findings.issue_text: OrderedQueueWorker.run() completes offsets in a finally block even when result_processor raises, causing failed messages to be committed and permanently lost (silent data loss); similar best-effort loss in SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit() when decoder raises or queue_pool.submit fails

SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.join() calls close() which shuts down the shared FixedQueuePool created in ResultsStrategyFactory, breaking all future strategies after a rebalance since they get a dead pool that drops and commits every message
terminate() drains the entire queue backlog (immediate=False) instead of terminating promptly, skipping final offset commit so drained work is replayed on restart; should use immediate=True
close() stops the commit thread before draining the pool, so offsets completed by workers after the commit thread's final pass are never committed, causing duplicate processing on restart

get_queue_for_group uses per-process salted hash(group_key) % num_queues, which is only safe single-process; no guard or documentation prevents combining thread-queue-parallel with --processes N > 1, a latent sharding footgun

Off-by-one offset convention (highest processed vs next-to-read) is split between OffsetTracker and the closure in create_thread_queue_parallel_worker, with the +1 applied in result_consumer.py; if moved or a second caller passes raw Kafka offsets, messages could be skipped or replayed

Unbounded queue growth: FixedQueuePool queues are created without maxsize and submit() puts unconditionally, so no real backpressure despite docstring claim, leading to OOM under consumer-group lag; fix by passing maxsize and using blocking put

OffsetTracker state grows unboundedly when any offset is stuck (dead worker thread or rebalance): all_offsets and outstanding grow forever, and get_committable_offsets does an O(N) range scan per partition per second with the partition lock held

Failed messages are marked complete and their offsets committed: OrderedQueueWorker.run's finally block calls complete_offset even when result_processor raised, silently dropping data and advancing consumer position past failed messages

Graceful shutdown drains nothing: FixedQueuePool.shutdown with Queue.shutdown(immediate=False) causes blocked get() to raise ShutDown, so workers exit without draining queued items and offsets never complete or commit
Per-message sentry_sdk.start_transaction in the worker hot path adds significant per-item CPU/allocation overhead and creates a large volume of transaction objects
wait_until_empty busy-polls at 100 Hz and is dead code; join on worker threads would be the correct primitive

FixedQueuePool created once in ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__ and shared across create_with_partitions calls, so on partition rebalance the strategy closes and shuts down the pool, leaving the new strategy with a dead pool whose workers have shutdown=True and shut-down queues, silently disabling the consumer; pool lifecycle must belong to the strategy (per create_with_partitions), not the factory
Stale shared OffsetTracker state: a second create_with_partitions shares stale last_committed state from the previous assignment

Failed messages are marked complete and committed — OrderedQueueWorker.run's finally block calls complete_offset when result_processor raises, and SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit marks offset complete on decoder exceptions — causing silent data loss with no retry, dead-letter, or failure metric distinguishing failed vs. succeeded processing; contradicts the strategy docstring 'Only commits offsets after successful processing'

No backpressure: queue.Queue() is unbounded and submit returns immediately after put(), so if workers fall behind, memory in OffsetTracker.all_offsets and the queues grows without limit, causing slow OOM / crash loop under sustained backlog; need bounded queues blocking on put, or expose outstanding-offset backlog for arroyo consumer pause on lag

join() doesn't drain: join() just calls close(), which immediately sets shutdown event and shuts down queues, abandoning queued-but-unprocessed items with no drain attempt and no final commit of completed work
join(timeout) accepts and ignores its timeout parameter
terminate() never joins the commit thread, so a commit could race process teardown
worker.join(timeout=5.0) results are ignored — if a worker is stuck in result_processor, shutdown proceeds and the daemon thread is killed mid-write

Silent stall if a worker thread dies: no worker-liveness check (worker.is_alive()), health metric for worker death, or watchdog; ordering pins all groups hashed to that queue, so those subscriptions never process again and all commits for that partition are gap-blocked forever

OffsetTracker.all_offsets unbounded growth when a gap never fills: entries only pruned by mark_committed which advances past contiguous prefix, so stuck/never-completed offsets grow the set for the life of the process, and get_committable_offsets iterates the full min..max range on every 1s commit tick — an O(range) scan holding a GIL-holding lock

submit's broad catch-all exception handler (including grouping_fn and queue_pool.submit/put) marks offset complete for any error including programming errors in grouping_fn or queue.ShutDown from pool death, permanently skipping messages on transient infrastructure errors; narrow the try to the decoder and add an explicit failure metric

test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling: test asserts committed_offsets does not contain the partition, but queue_consumer.py's worker finally block marks failed offsets complete, so the assertion will fail or masks a genuine P0 data-loss behavior where failed messages are committed and never reprocessed

ProcessResultThreadQueueParallelTest subclass never runs the existing ProcessResultTest behavioral suite against thread-queue-parallel mode, leaving zero real handle_result→DB coverage for the production-intended mode

Thread-queue-parallel tests (including the Kafka integration test) mock the processor's __call__ and only verify callback invocation, never asserting actual UptimeStatusCheck/group status behavior; the Kafka test's 'if commits_made:' guard silently skips offset assertions and passes even with wrong offsets committed

test_different_groups_distributed asserts len(queue_indices) == 3 but relies on salted Python hash() which can non-deterministically collide across CI runs; should use a deterministic hash like zlib.crc32 or not assert full coverage
Race in test_stats_reporting: test asserts stats['total_items'] > 0 immediately after submitting 10 items, but concurrent workers may drain the queues before get_stats() runs, causing flakiness

test_thread_queue_parallel_graceful_shutdown only asserts factory.queue_pool is None; it never verifies the 5 submitted items were processed or that final offsets were committed, and close() joins the commit thread before draining the queue so the last offsets are never committed (at-most-once/data-replay gap with zero test coverage)
No test coverage for terminate(), wait_until_empty, commit-loop exception handling, or decoder raising in submit's except Exception path

Commit-event race in test_offset_committing: commit_event is set on the first commit, so the test can assert committed_offsets[partition] == 104 before the follow-up commit occurs, flaking on slow CI; should wait for the expected value

Dependency on Python 3.13-only stdlib API: queue.Queue.shutdown()/queue.ShutDown used in queue_consumer.py without any runtime version guard; on older interpreters q.shutdown raises AttributeError silently swallowed by except Exception, leaving workers blocked forever

Failed messages are still marked complete: OrderedQueueWorker.run() unconditionally calls offset_tracker.complete_offset() in the finally block, contradicting the docstring promise to only commit offsets after successful processing, causing silent data loss
Test test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling only passes due to a race with the 1-second commit loop, making it flaky and encoding the wrong expectation that committed_offsets stays empty

OffsetTracker is never cleaned up on partition rebalance/revocation: FixedQueuePool and its tracker are constructed once in ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__ and shared across strategies, so revoked partitions' offsets remain and get committed after rebalance
join() is implemented as close() in SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy, violating arroyo's graceful-shutdown protocol (close then join), causing double close and queues never drained under supervision

Constructor side effects: FixedQueuePool.__init__ and SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.__init__ spawn background threads, making factory construction (e.g. MockFactory in tests) spawn 20 threads; thread lifecycle should be owned by explicit start/create_with_partitions

Hardcoded 'monitors' namespace in generic remote_subscriptions module: transaction name f"monitors.{self.identifier}.worker_{...}" leaks uptime-specific naming; identifier alone would preserve the abstraction
Dead field: WorkItem.message is populated but never read in production code; speculative or should be removed
Dead method: FixedQueuePool.wait_until_empty defined with a 5s busy-wait loop but never called by production code; also racy since qsize()==0 doesn't mean processing finished

Test hits private StreamProcessor internals and monkeypatches factory (processor._run_once(), processor._shutdown(), assigning factory.create_with_partitions), which will break on arroyo upgrades and bypasses the public factory extension point
Duplicated busy-wait polling loop (for _ in range(max_wait): ... time.sleep(0.1)) copy-pasted across five new tests in test_results_consumer.py; should be extracted into a shared helper

Processing failure still commits the offset in OrderedQueueWorker.run: the finally block calls offset_tracker.complete_offset unconditionally even when result_processor raised, silently dropping messages and contradicting the docstring guarantee of committing only after successful processing

Exception path in strategy.submit silently swallows exceptions from decode or queue_pool.submit and marks the offset complete, dropping messages without a deliberate dead-letter policy; filtered messages also funnel through this log-and-drop path due to the assert on FilteredPayload
Error-handling test only passes due to a timing race (commit loop tick vs sleep) and validates nothing about failure handling, rubber-stamping the broken failure semantics

SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.join() re-invokes close(), which sets shutdown_event, joins the commit thread, then drains the queue pool — items completed during drain are never committed, causing duplicate side effects on redelivery; double close/join also re-calls q.shutdown on already-shutdown queues, masking errors
No backpressure despite the docstring claim: queue.Queue is unbounded and submit never blocks, so if processing is slower than consumption memory grows until OOM (no maxsize or bounded poll/pause)
get_committable_offsets requires contiguous offsets, so messages never seen by strategy.submit (filtering, restart mid-batch) create offset gaps that stall commits forever with no error or metric

terminate() never joins the commit thread, so the daemon thread can die mid-commit leaving consumer group state inconsistent with last_committed; close/terminate both call queue_pool.shutdown causing double-shutdown
wait_until_empty's qsize()==0 check ignores in-flight items, and tests gating on total_items==0 as 'processed' can pass before processing completes

OffsetTracker.last_committed ignores actual start offsets (initializes at -1 while consumption may resume at 5000); if first seen offset is below the true resume point, commit_offsets' +1 can rewind the consumer group
hash() on str is process-randomized, which would silently break queue-assignment distribution if moving to multiprocessing or persisting assignments
WorkItem.message retained per queued item needlessly inflates memory given the offset tracker already carries commit state

adjudication_records.issue_text: OrderedQueueWorker.run() completes offsets in a finally block even when result_processor raises, causing failed messages to be committed and permanently lost (silent data loss); similar best-effort loss in SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit() when decoder raises or queue_pool.submit fails

adjudication.rationale: In `OrderedQueueWorker.run()`, `self.offset_tracker.complete_offset(work_item.partition, work_item.offset)` is executed in the `finally` block regardless of whether `self.result_processor(...)` succeeded or raised (exceptions are caught/logged, but the offset is still marked completed). Since `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy._commit_loop()` commits any offsets that are no longer outstanding, this can advance committed offsets past failed processing, effectively dropping messages. Similarly, in `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit()`, if `decoder(...)` raises (or any exception in the submit path occurs), the `except` handler calls `add_offset` and `complete_offset`, making the message immediately committable even though it was not processed. This contradicts the stated guarantee in the strategy docstring ('Only commits offsets after successful processing') and is verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.join() calls close() which shuts down the shared FixedQueuePool created in ResultsStrategyFactory, breaking all future strategies after a rebalance since they get a dead pool that drops and commits every message

adjudication.rationale: In `ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__`, a single `FixedQueuePool` is created and stored on the factory (`self.queue_pool = FixedQueuePool(...)`) for `mode == "thread-queue-parallel"`, and `create_thread_queue_parallel_worker` passes that same pool into each new `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` (`queue_pool=self.queue_pool`). However, `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` (and thus `join()`, which calls `close()`) unconditionally calls `self.queue_pool.shutdown()`. The factory does not reset/recreate `self.queue_pool` when a strategy is closed, so any subsequent strategy created by the same factory will reuse a shutdown pool (workers stopped / queues shutdown). That can lead to messages failing to enqueue and being marked complete in `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit`'s broad `except Exception` path, allowing offsets to advance without processing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: terminate() drains the entire queue backlog (immediate=False) instead of terminating promptly, skipping final offset commit so drained work is replayed on restart; should use immediate=True

adjudication.rationale: In `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.terminate()` the code sets `shutdown_event` and immediately calls `self.queue_pool.shutdown()`. `FixedQueuePool.shutdown()` sets `worker.shutdown = True` but then calls `q.shutdown(immediate=False)` for each queue and joins workers, which will allow queued items to continue being processed (i.e., drain backlog rather than terminate promptly). At the same time, `terminate()` does not join or flush the commit thread, and the commit loop exits when `shutdown_event` is set, so offsets for work that finishes during this draining shutdown may never be committed, leading to replay on restart. The finding’s suggestion to use `immediate=True` in the terminate path is consistent with the diff-grounded problem (terminate not prompt + potential uncommitted processed work).

adjudication_records.issue_text: close() stops the commit thread before draining the pool, so offsets completed by workers after the commit thread's final pass are never committed, causing duplicate processing on restart

adjudication.rationale: In `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()`, the shutdown sequence is `shutdown_event.set()` -> `commit_thread.join()` -> `queue_pool.shutdown()`. The commit loop (`_commit_loop`) exits when `shutdown_event` is set (it will not run further iterations after the current one), but worker threads in `FixedQueuePool` may still be processing queued items and calling `offset_tracker.complete_offset(...)` after the commit thread has stopped. Since there is no drain/wait step (e.g., `wait_until_empty`) before stopping the commit thread, offsets that become committable after the commit thread’s final pass will never be committed, leading to potential duplicate processing on restart.

adjudication_records.issue_text: get_queue_for_group uses per-process salted hash(group_key) % num_queues, which is only safe single-process; no guard or documentation prevents combining thread-queue-parallel with --processes N > 1, a latent sharding footgun

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `FixedQueuePool.get_queue_for_group` using Python’s built-in `hash(group_key) % self.num_queues` (queue_consumer.py), which is process-salted and not stable across processes/restarts, despite the docstring calling it “consistent hashing.” The diff also exposes the new `thread-queue-parallel` mode via CLI choice while leaving a `--processes` option present with no guard/documentation about interactions. However, nothing in the diff proves this causes incorrect behavior (each process would have its own queue pool; Kafka partitions are assigned per consumer), so it’s more of a latent configuration/architecture footgun than a verified defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Off-by-one offset convention (highest processed vs next-to-read) is split between OffsetTracker and the closure in create_thread_queue_parallel_worker, with the +1 applied in result_consumer.py; if moved or a second caller passes raw Kafka offsets, messages could be skipped or replayed

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows OffsetTracker/SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy operating on raw Kafka message offsets (e.g., OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets returns the highest processed offset), while ResultsStrategyFactory.create_thread_queue_parallel_worker applies the Kafka "next-to-read" convention by adding +1 before calling the Arroyo/Kafka commit callback (`commit_data = {partition: offset + 1 ...}`). This split convention is real and could be error-prone for future callers (e.g., if another strategy reused SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy but passed a commit function that expects already-+1 offsets), but in this diff it is applied consistently and tests assert the intended behaviors (unit test expects 104 without +1; integration test expects 105 with +1).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded queue growth: FixedQueuePool queues are created without maxsize and submit() puts unconditionally, so no real backpressure despite docstring claim, leading to OOM under consumer-group lag; fix by passing maxsize and using blocking put

adjudication.rationale: In `FixedQueuePool.__init__`, each work queue is created as `queue.Queue()` with no `maxsize` (unbounded). In `FixedQueuePool.submit`, items are enqueued via `work_queue.put(work_item)` without any capacity limit, so `put()` will not apply backpressure and the queue can grow without bound. This contradicts the `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` docstring claim of “Natural backpressure when queues fill up” and can lead to unbounded memory growth/OOM if production outpaces processing (e.g., consumer lag).

adjudication_records.issue_text: OffsetTracker state grows unboundedly when any offset is stuck (dead worker thread or rebalance): all_offsets and outstanding grow forever, and get_committable_offsets does an O(N) range scan per partition per second with the partition lock held

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `OffsetTracker`, `add_offset` appends every seen offset into `all_offsets[partition]` and `outstanding[partition]`. Progress/cleanup only happens via `mark_committed`, which prunes `all_offsets` only for offsets `<= committed`, and commits cannot advance past a single stuck offset (`outstanding` never cleared). If any offset is never completed (e.g., worker thread dies after `add_offset`, or work is dropped), then commits stall and subsequent offsets will accumulate forever in `all_offsets`/`outstanding` with no eviction path. Additionally, `get_committable_offsets` iterates `for offset in range(start, max_offset + 1)` while holding the per-partition lock, making it an O(N) scan per partition per call (commit loop runs every ~1s) and this cost grows with the unbounded max offset range.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Failed messages are marked complete and their offsets committed: OrderedQueueWorker.run's finally block calls complete_offset even when result_processor raised, silently dropping data and advancing consumer position past failed messages

adjudication.rationale: In `OrderedQueueWorker.run`, the `finally` block unconditionally calls `self.offset_tracker.complete_offset(work_item.partition, work_item.offset)` even if `self.result_processor(...)` raised and was caught/logged. Since `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy._commit_loop` commits any offsets that are no longer outstanding, a failed work item can become committable and have its offset advanced, effectively dropping that message without retry while moving the consumer position forward.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Graceful shutdown drains nothing: FixedQueuePool.shutdown with Queue.shutdown(immediate=False) causes blocked get() to raise ShutDown, so workers exit without draining queued items and offsets never complete or commit

adjudication.rationale: In `FixedQueuePool.shutdown`, it sets `worker.shutdown = True` for all workers before attempting to drain queues. Because `OrderedQueueWorker.run` loops as `while not self.shutdown: work_item = self.work_queue.get() ...`, once a worker finishes its current item it will exit the loop and stop consuming further queued items even if `work_queue` still contains `WorkItem`s. This can leave items unprocessed, meaning `offset_tracker.complete_offset(...)` is never called for those offsets, and `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` additionally stops the commit thread (`shutdown_event.set()` + `commit_thread.join()`) before calling `queue_pool.shutdown()`, so outstanding offsets may never be committed. The finding’s specific claim about `Queue.shutdown(immediate=False)` forcing immediate `ShutDown` even with pending items is not strictly verified from the diff, but the core “shutdown can abandon queued work and prevent offset completion/commit” behavior is directly implied by the `worker.shutdown` flag check and shutdown ordering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Per-message sentry_sdk.start_transaction in the worker hot path adds significant per-item CPU/allocation overhead and creates a large volume of transaction objects

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `OrderedQueueWorker.run` hot path (src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py), each dequeued `WorkItem` is wrapped in `with sentry_sdk.start_transaction(...)` before calling `self.result_processor(...)`. This is per-message instrumentation and will create a transaction object for every processed item, which can plausibly add CPU/allocation overhead and increase transaction volume. The diff shows this behavior directly; it’s a performance/observability concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: wait_until_empty busy-polls at 100 Hz and is dead code; join on worker threads would be the correct primitive

adjudication.rationale: In `FixedQueuePool.wait_until_empty` the implementation does busy-poll with `time.sleep(0.01)` in a loop (≈100Hz) until `get_stats()["total_items"] == 0`, which is a concrete, diff-grounded inefficiency/design concern. However, the claim that it is "dead code" cannot be verified from the diff alone (it is not referenced in the shown changes, but it could be used elsewhere). Also, the pool already uses `worker.join(timeout=5.0)` in `shutdown`, so the suggested primitive is partly already present. This is more of a performance/architecture issue than a clear correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: FixedQueuePool created once in ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__ and shared across create_with_partitions calls, so on partition rebalance the strategy closes and shuts down the pool, leaving the new strategy with a dead pool whose workers have shutdown=True and shut-down queues, silently disabling the consumer; pool lifecycle must belong to the strategy (per create_with_partitions), not the factory

adjudication.rationale: In `ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__`, when `mode == "thread-queue-parallel"` the factory creates a single `self.queue_pool = FixedQueuePool(...)` and `create_thread_queue_parallel_worker` passes that same instance into each new `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` (`queue_pool=self.queue_pool`). But `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` and `terminate()` unconditionally call `self.queue_pool.shutdown()`, which sets each worker’s `shutdown=True` and calls `q.shutdown(...)` on each queue. After a strategy is closed (e.g., due to partition rebalance), the factory still retains the now-shutdown `self.queue_pool` (it is only set to `None` in `ResultsStrategyFactory.shutdown()`, not when a strategy closes), so a subsequent `create_with_partitions` would reuse a dead pool/threads. This matches the finding and is a real lifecycle/correctness defect grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stale shared OffsetTracker state: a second create_with_partitions shares stale last_committed state from the previous assignment

adjudication.rationale: In `ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__`, `self.queue_pool = FixedQueuePool(...)` is created once for `mode == "thread-queue-parallel"` and then reused in every subsequent `create_with_partitions` call (`create_thread_queue_parallel_worker` passes the same `self.queue_pool` into each new `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy`). `FixedQueuePool` owns a single `OffsetTracker` whose `last_committed` (and `all_offsets`/`outstanding`) are never reset on new partition assignments. Therefore, a second `create_with_partitions` will share prior `last_committed` state, which can affect committable offset computation for the new assignment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Failed messages are marked complete and committed — OrderedQueueWorker.run's finally block calls complete_offset when result_processor raises, and SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit marks offset complete on decoder exceptions — causing silent data loss with no retry, dead-letter, or failure metric distinguishing failed vs. succeeded processing; contradicts the strategy docstring 'Only commits offsets after successful processing'

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows offsets are marked completed even when processing fails. In `OrderedQueueWorker.run`, `complete_offset(work_item.partition, work_item.offset)` is called in the `finally` block regardless of whether `result_processor(...)` raised an exception, so failed work becomes eligible for commit. The commit loop in `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy._commit_loop` then commits any offsets deemed committable by the `OffsetTracker`, which only checks whether offsets are no longer outstanding—not whether they succeeded. Additionally, `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit` catches broad `Exception` around decoding/submission and then `add_offset` + `complete_offset`, making decoder/submission failures also eligible for commit. This can lead to silent data loss and contradicts the strategy docstring claim 'Only commits offsets after successful processing.'

adjudication_records.issue_text: No backpressure: queue.Queue() is unbounded and submit returns immediately after put(), so if workers fall behind, memory in OffsetTracker.all_offsets and the queues grows without limit, causing slow OOM / crash loop under sustained backlog; need bounded queues blocking on put, or expose outstanding-offset backlog for arroyo consumer pause on lag

adjudication.rationale: The new thread-queue-parallel implementation uses `queue.Queue()` with no `maxsize` in `FixedQueuePool.__init__`, making each work queue unbounded. `FixedQueuePool.submit()` always does `work_queue.put(work_item)` (and `OffsetTracker.add_offset`) without any blocking/backpressure mechanism. Since the consumer can continue submitting faster than `OrderedQueueWorker.run()` can drain, both the per-queue buffers and `OffsetTracker.all_offsets/outstanding` can grow without bound until commit catches up, risking memory blowup/OOM under sustained backlog. This also contradicts the strategy docstring claim of “Natural backpressure when queues fill up.”

adjudication_records.issue_text: join() doesn't drain: join() just calls close(), which immediately sets shutdown event and shuts down queues, abandoning queued-but-unprocessed items with no drain attempt and no final commit of completed work

adjudication.rationale: In `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.join()` it just calls `close()`, and `close()` immediately sets `shutdown_event`, joins the commit thread, and shuts down the queue pool. This can abandon queued work: `FixedQueuePool.shutdown()` sets `worker.shutdown = True` before calling `q.shutdown(immediate=False)`, and `OrderedQueueWorker.run()` loops `while not self.shutdown`, so workers will stop after at most the current item and will not drain remaining queued items. Also, the commit thread’s loop is `while not self.shutdown_event.is_set()`: once `close()` sets the event, the commit loop exits without a final commit pass, so offsets for already-completed work may never be committed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: join(timeout) accepts and ignores its timeout parameter

adjudication.rationale: In `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.join(self, timeout: float | None = None)`, the `timeout` parameter is accepted but never used; the method unconditionally calls `self.close()` (which joins the commit thread with a hardcoded `timeout=5.0` and shuts down the pool). This means callers cannot control blocking duration via `join(timeout)`, which is incorrect behavior for a `join` method that advertises a timeout parameter.

adjudication_records.issue_text: terminate() never joins the commit thread, so a commit could race process teardown

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy`, `__init__` starts a background `commit_thread` (`threading.Thread(target=self._commit_loop, daemon=True)`). `close()` correctly sets `shutdown_event` and then `self.commit_thread.join(timeout=5.0)`, but `terminate()` only sets `shutdown_event` and shuts down the `queue_pool` and never joins the `commit_thread` (`def terminate(self): self.shutdown_event.set(); self.queue_pool.shutdown()`). Since `_commit_loop` wakes on `wait(1.0)` and may still run briefly after `terminate()` returns, it can race teardown and call `commit_function` while the processor/consumer is shutting down.

adjudication_records.issue_text: worker.join(timeout=5.0) results are ignored — if a worker is stuck in result_processor, shutdown proceeds and the daemon thread is killed mid-write

adjudication.rationale: In `FixedQueuePool.shutdown()`, workers are daemon threads (`OrderedQueueWorker(..., daemon=True)`) and are only joined with `worker.join(timeout=5.0)` without checking whether they actually exited. If a worker is blocked inside `result_processor(...)`, it will not respond to `worker.shutdown = True` and may still be running after `shutdown()` returns. This makes shutdown potentially non-graceful and can leave background work running until process exit (at which point daemon threads can be terminated abruptly), but the diff does not prove an immediate functional failure during normal processing—it's a shutdown robustness/contract issue rather than a guaranteed correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silent stall if a worker thread dies: no worker-liveness check (worker.is_alive()), health metric for worker death, or watchdog; ordering pins all groups hashed to that queue, so those subscriptions never process again and all commits for that partition are gap-blocked forever

adjudication.rationale: In the new thread-queue-parallel implementation, each queue has exactly one daemon worker thread (OrderedQueueWorker) and groups are pinned to a queue via `hash(group_key) % num_queues` (`FixedQueuePool.get_queue_for_group`). There is no liveness/watchdog check anywhere (no `is_alive()` checks, no restart logic, no health metric on thread death). While the worker wraps `result_processor` in a try/except, the `finally` block is not protected: if `self.offset_tracker.complete_offset(...)` or `metrics.gauge(...)` raises, the exception will escape `run()` and the thread will die. Once a worker thread dies, items assigned to that queue will stop being processed (silent stall), leaving their offsets outstanding in `OffsetTracker`, and `get_committable_offsets()` will not advance commits past those offsets (gap-blocking). The diff shows no mechanism to detect or recover from this state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OffsetTracker.all_offsets unbounded growth when a gap never fills: entries only pruned by mark_committed which advances past contiguous prefix, so stuck/never-completed offsets grow the set for the life of the process, and get_committable_offsets iterates the full min..max range on every 1s commit tick — an O(range) scan holding a GIL-holding lock

adjudication.rationale: In the new `OffsetTracker`, `all_offsets[partition]` is only pruned in `mark_committed` (which only runs after a successful commit). If the lowest outstanding offset in a partition never completes (e.g., a stuck work item or shutdown leaving items unprocessed), `get_committable_offsets` will always return `{}` and `mark_committed` will never run, so `all_offsets` can grow without bound as more offsets are `add_offset`’d. The finding’s specific claim that `get_committable_offsets` always scans the full `min..max` range on every tick is overstated (it breaks on the first missing or outstanding offset), but the unbounded growth/resource-risk concern is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: submit's broad catch-all exception handler (including grouping_fn and queue_pool.submit/put) marks offset complete for any error including programming errors in grouping_fn or queue.ShutDown from pool death, permanently skipping messages on transient infrastructure errors; narrow the try to the decoder and add an explicit failure metric

adjudication.rationale: In `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit` (new in `queue_consumer.py`), the `try` covers decoding, `grouping_fn`, and `self.queue_pool.submit(...)` (which does `work_queue.put`). The broad `except Exception:` logs and then unconditionally `add_offset`+`complete_offset` for the message’s partition/offset, which makes the offset eligible for commit despite the work not being enqueued/processed. This can skip messages on errors in `grouping_fn` or on queue shutdown/pool failure (they explicitly use `queue.ShutDown` elsewhere), contradicting the stated guarantee “Only commits offsets after successful processing.”

adjudication_records.issue_text: test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling: test asserts committed_offsets does not contain the partition, but queue_consumer.py's worker finally block marks failed offsets complete, so the assertion will fail or masks a genuine P0 data-loss behavior where failed messages are committed and never reprocessed

adjudication.rationale: In `OrderedQueueWorker.run`, the `finally` block unconditionally calls `self.offset_tracker.complete_offset(work_item.partition, work_item.offset)` even if `result_processor(...)` raised (caught by `except Exception`). Since `FixedQueuePool.submit` already called `offset_tracker.add_offset(...)`, the commit loop (`SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy._commit_loop`) can then consider failed offsets “processed” and commit them, causing failed messages to be acknowledged/never reprocessed (data loss). This also means `test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling`’s expectation that the partition is not committed is inconsistent with the implementation and would likely fail if the commit loop runs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ProcessResultThreadQueueParallelTest subclass never runs the existing ProcessResultTest behavioral suite against thread-queue-parallel mode, leaving zero real handle_result→DB coverage for the production-intended mode

adjudication.rationale: In `tests/sentry/uptime/consumers/test_results_consumer.py`, the existing pattern of running the shared `ProcessResultTest` suite under a mode-specific subclass exists for parallel mode (`class ProcessResultParallelTest(ProcessResultTest): strategy_processing_mode = "parallel"`), but no analogous subclass is added for `strategy_processing_mode = "thread-queue-parallel"`. The newly added thread-queue-parallel tests mostly patch `type(factory.result_processor).__call__`, so they validate ordering/commit behavior but don’t exercise the same end-to-end `handle_result`/DB assertions that the shared `ProcessResultTest` suite likely provides for other modes. This is a concrete coverage gap introduced by adding the new production mode without wiring it into the existing behavioral suite, but it’s not itself a production defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Thread-queue-parallel tests (including the Kafka integration test) mock the processor's __call__ and only verify callback invocation, never asserting actual UptimeStatusCheck/group status behavior; the Kafka test's 'if commits_made:' guard silently skips offset assertions and passes even with wrong offsets committed

adjudication.rationale: The new uptime thread-queue-parallel tests frequently patch `type(factory.result_processor).__call__` and mainly assert call counts/order (e.g. `test_thread_queue_parallel`, `test_thread_queue_parallel_preserves_order`, `test_thread_queue_parallel_concurrent_subscriptions`), so they do not exercise/validate the real `ResultProcessor` side effects like creating `UptimeStatusCheck` rows or updating `Group` status. However, the claim that the Kafka integration test can “silently skip offset assertions” due to `if commits_made:` is not supported: `commit_count >= 1` is asserted first, and the tracked commit wrapper appends to `commits_made`, and the test also asserts the committed offset from Kafka via `verify_consumer.committed(...)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: test_different_groups_distributed asserts len(queue_indices) == 3 but relies on salted Python hash() which can non-deterministically collide across CI runs; should use a deterministic hash like zlib.crc32 or not assert full coverage

adjudication.rationale: In `FixedQueuePool.get_queue_for_group` the queue index is computed as `hash(group_key) % self.num_queues`. Python’s built-in `hash()` for strings is randomized per process (hash seed), so the mapping of `group{i}` to the 3 queues varies across runs. The test `test_different_groups_distributed` in `tests/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/test_queue_consumer.py` asserts `len(queue_indices) == 3` after hashing 20 keys, which is not guaranteed for every hash seed (it could hit only 1–2 buckets), making the test potentially flaky across CI runs. Using a deterministic hash or weakening the assertion would avoid this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Race in test_stats_reporting: test asserts stats['total_items'] > 0 immediately after submitting 10 items, but concurrent workers may drain the queues before get_stats() runs, causing flakiness

adjudication.rationale: In `TestFixedQueuePool.test_stats_reporting`, after submitting 10 items via `self.pool.submit(...)`, the test immediately calls `stats = self.pool.get_stats()` and asserts `stats["total_items"] > 0`. But `FixedQueuePool` starts worker threads in its constructor (`OrderedQueueWorker.start()`), and those workers can drain the queues concurrently while the test thread is still submitting items or before `get_stats()` executes. Since `get_stats()` is just `q.qsize()` sums, it can legitimately return 0 if workers have already processed everything, making the `> 0` assertion flaky.

adjudication_records.issue_text: test_thread_queue_parallel_graceful_shutdown only asserts factory.queue_pool is None; it never verifies the 5 submitted items were processed or that final offsets were committed, and close() joins the commit thread before draining the queue so the last offsets are never committed (at-most-once/data-replay gap with zero test coverage)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` which calls `self.shutdown_event.set()` and then `self.commit_thread.join(...)` **before** shutting down the `FixedQueuePool` (and its workers). Since the commit loop is the only place offsets are committed (`_commit_loop`), stopping/joining it first means any offsets that become committable while workers finish (or are shut down) will not be committed. Additionally, `FixedQueuePool.shutdown()` sets `worker.shutdown = True` before shutting down queues, so workers may exit their `while not self.shutdown` loop without draining pending items. The cited test `test_thread_queue_parallel_graceful_shutdown` indeed only asserts `factory.queue_pool is None` after `factory.shutdown()` and does not verify the 5 submitted items were processed nor that offsets were committed, leaving this shutdown/commit behavior untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test coverage for terminate(), wait_until_empty, commit-loop exception handling, or decoder raising in submit's except Exception path

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new, nontrivial behaviors that are not exercised by the new tests: `FixedQueuePool.wait_until_empty` is implemented but never called in `tests/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/test_queue_consumer.py` or the uptime tests; `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.terminate()` is implemented but tests only call `close()`/`factory.shutdown()`; the commit loop (`SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy._commit_loop`) has an exception-handling path (`except Exception: logger.exception(...)`) that is not tested; and `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit()` has an `except Exception` fallback intended to handle failures (including decoder failures), but existing tests only cover `FilteredPayload` returning `None`, not a decoder raising an exception.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Commit-event race in test_offset_committing: commit_event is set on the first commit, so the test can assert committed_offsets[partition] == 104 before the follow-up commit occurs, flaking on slow CI; should wait for the expected value

adjudication.rationale: In `tests/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/test_queue_consumer.py::TestSimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.test_offset_committing`, `commit_event` is set in `commit_function` on *any* commit. The strategy’s `_commit_loop` runs periodically and can commit intermediate offsets as messages complete. Since the test only waits for `process_complete_event` (all items processed) and then waits for `commit_event` (which may already be set from an earlier partial commit), it can assert `self.committed_offsets[partition] == 104` before the follow-up commit that advances the offset to 104 occurs, causing flakes on slow CI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dependency on Python 3.13-only stdlib API: queue.Queue.shutdown()/queue.ShutDown used in queue_consumer.py without any runtime version guard; on older interpreters q.shutdown raises AttributeError silently swallowed by except Exception, leaving workers blocked forever

adjudication.rationale: The new implementation relies on `queue.Queue.shutdown(immediate=False)` and catching `queue.ShutDown` in `OrderedQueueWorker.run`. If these APIs are unavailable at runtime (as the finding notes for pre-3.13), `FixedQueuePool.shutdown` will hit `AttributeError` and swallow it (`except Exception`), so no sentinel/shutdown signal is delivered to unblock `work_queue.get()`. Since workers only check `self.shutdown` in the loop condition and can be blocked in `get()`, they may not exit, and `join(timeout=5.0)` can return with threads still alive.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Failed messages are still marked complete: OrderedQueueWorker.run() unconditionally calls offset_tracker.complete_offset() in the finally block, contradicting the docstring promise to only commit offsets after successful processing, causing silent data loss

adjudication.rationale: In `OrderedQueueWorker.run()`, `offset_tracker.complete_offset(work_item.partition, work_item.offset)` is executed in the `finally` block regardless of whether `result_processor(...)` succeeded or raised an exception. Exceptions are caught and only logged, with no re-queue/retry mechanism. Since `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy._commit_loop()` commits any offsets that are no longer outstanding, a failed processing attempt will still make the offset committable and eventually committed, which can drop the message. This contradicts the strategy docstring claim: "Only commits offsets after successful processing".

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling only passes due to a race with the 1-second commit loop, making it flaky and encoding the wrong expectation that committed_offsets stays empty

adjudication.rationale: In `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy`, commits happen asynchronously in `_commit_loop` every ~1s (`shutdown_event.wait(1.0)`), and `OrderedQueueWorker.run` calls `offset_tracker.complete_offset(...)` in `finally` even when `result_processor` raises. That makes offsets committable and likely to be committed despite processing errors. The test `test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling` asserts `committed_offsets` stays empty after processing completes, but it does not control/synchronize with the commit thread; depending on timing it may observe commits (especially since its loop can run >1s), making the test expectation both incorrect for the implemented behavior and race/flaky.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OffsetTracker is never cleaned up on partition rebalance/revocation: FixedQueuePool and its tracker are constructed once in ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__ and shared across strategies, so revoked partitions' offsets remain and get committed after rebalance

adjudication.rationale: In `ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__`, `self.queue_pool = FixedQueuePool(...)` is constructed once for `mode == "thread-queue-parallel"` and then reused in `create_thread_queue_parallel_worker` for any subsequent `create_with_partitions` call (`assert self.queue_pool is not None`). `OffsetTracker` inside `FixedQueuePool` stores per-`Partition` offset state (`all_offsets`, `outstanding`, `last_committed`) and has no API/path to clear state for partitions that are no longer assigned/revoked. `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy._commit_loop` commits whatever `get_committable_offsets()` returns, so stale partitions can remain eligible for commit. The diff shows no rebalance/revocation cleanup, making the finding valid and correctness-impacting in a rebalance scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: join() is implemented as close() in SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy, violating arroyo's graceful-shutdown protocol (close then join), causing double close and queues never drained under supervision

adjudication.rationale: In `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy`, `join(self, timeout)` is implemented as `self.close()` (see `def join(...): self.close()` in the new `queue_consumer.py`). That means a framework that follows a `close(); join()` lifecycle will effectively invoke shutdown logic twice. The diff shows this structural lifecycle mismatch, but the specific claim that it "causes double close and queues never drained under supervision" depends on Arroyo’s external contract/behavior, which is not shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Constructor side effects: FixedQueuePool.__init__ and SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.__init__ spawn background threads, making factory construction (e.g. MockFactory in tests) spawn 20 threads; thread lifecycle should be owned by explicit start/create_with_partitions

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows constructor side effects that make thread lifecycle implicit: `FixedQueuePool.__init__` creates `num_queues` `queue.Queue()` objects and immediately `worker.start()`s an `OrderedQueueWorker` per queue (default `num_queues=20`). `ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__` constructs a `FixedQueuePool` when `mode == "thread-queue-parallel"` (`num_queues=max_workers or 20`), so merely instantiating the factory in that mode spawns threads. Separately, `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.__init__` starts a background `commit_thread` immediately. While the finding slightly overstates that strategy construction happens during factory construction (it occurs in `create_thread_queue_parallel_worker`), the underlying lifecycle/architecture concern is real and grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hardcoded 'monitors' namespace in generic remote_subscriptions module: transaction name f"monitors.{self.identifier}.worker_{...}" leaks uptime-specific naming; identifier alone would preserve the abstraction

adjudication.rationale: In the new generic remote_subscriptions queue consumer (src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py), OrderedQueueWorker.run starts a Sentry transaction with name=f"monitors.{self.identifier}.worker_{self.worker_id}". The hardcoded "monitors" prefix is uptime/monitors-domain-specific and reduces the module’s generality; using just the identifier (or a configurable prefix) would better preserve abstraction. This is an architecture/naming concern rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead field: WorkItem.message is populated but never read in production code; speculative or should be removed

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `WorkItem` dataclass (`src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py`), the `message: Message[...]` field is always populated when creating a `WorkItem` in `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit(...)`, but it is never read anywhere in production code: `OrderedQueueWorker.run()` only uses `work_item.result`, and offset tracking uses `partition`/`offset`. No other code references `work_item.message`. This is a real diff-grounded cleanup/maintenance concern (extra memory/complexity) but not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead method: FixedQueuePool.wait_until_empty defined with a 5s busy-wait loop but never called by production code; also racy since qsize()==0 doesn't mean processing finished

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `FixedQueuePool.wait_until_empty` (busy-waiting up to 5s on `get_stats()["total_items"] == 0`), but no production code paths shown call it (the strategy uses a commit thread and `shutdown()`/`close()`; tests poll `get_stats()` directly). So the “dead method” part is supported by the diff. The note about raciness is also grounded: `total_items` is computed from `q.qsize()`, and an empty queue does not guarantee the worker has finished processing the last dequeued item. This is a specific maintainability/correctness concern, but not a demonstrated defect since the method is unused.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test hits private StreamProcessor internals and monkeypatches factory (processor._run_once(), processor._shutdown(), assigning factory.create_with_partitions), which will break on arroyo upgrades and bypasses the public factory extension point

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a Kafka integration test `ProcessResultThreadQueueParallelKafkaTest.test_thread_queue_parallel_kafka_offset_commit` that directly calls private methods `processor._run_once()` and `processor._shutdown()` on `StreamProcessor`, and monkeypatches the factory by assigning `factory.create_with_partitions = create_with_partitions_tracking`. These are verifiable in the diff and create a brittle test tied to arroyo internals and bypass the normal factory extension point; it’s a maintainability/upgrade-risk issue rather than a functional defect in production code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicated busy-wait polling loop (for _ in range(max_wait): ... time.sleep(0.1)) copy-pasted across five new tests in test_results_consumer.py; should be extracted into a shared helper

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show repeated polling loops with `for _ in range(max_wait): ... time.sleep(0.1)` across multiple newly added tests in `tests/sentry/uptime/consumers/test_results_consumer.py` (e.g., `test_thread_queue_parallel`, `test_thread_queue_parallel_preserves_order`, `test_thread_queue_parallel_concurrent_subscriptions`, `test_thread_queue_parallel_offset_commit`, etc.). However, the finding is a refactor/DRY suggestion about test code duplication, not a verifiable defect or substantial review issue introduced by the change; it's essentially a style/maintainability nit.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Processing failure still commits the offset in OrderedQueueWorker.run: the finally block calls offset_tracker.complete_offset unconditionally even when result_processor raised, silently dropping messages and contradicting the docstring guarantee of committing only after successful processing

adjudication.rationale: In `OrderedQueueWorker.run`, `offset_tracker.complete_offset(...)` is called in the `finally` block unconditionally, including when `result_processor(...)` raises (caught by `except Exception`). Since `FixedQueuePool.submit` already `add_offset(...)` before enqueueing, a failed work item will still be marked complete and can become committable in `_commit_loop`, leading to committing offsets for unprocessed/failed messages (data loss) and contradicting the stated guarantee in `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` docstring.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Exception path in strategy.submit silently swallows exceptions from decode or queue_pool.submit and marks the offset complete, dropping messages without a deliberate dead-letter policy; filtered messages also funnel through this log-and-drop path due to the assert on FilteredPayload

adjudication.rationale: In `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit`, any exception from `self.decoder(message.payload)` or later (e.g. `grouping_fn`, `queue_pool.submit`) is caught by a broad `except Exception`, logged, and then the code calls `offset_tracker.add_offset(...)` + `complete_offset(...)` (when `message.value` is a `BrokerValue`). This makes the offset committable even though the message was not successfully decoded/processed, which can lead to message loss without retry/DLQ semantics. Additionally, when the factory passes `decoder=partial(self.decode_payload, ...)`, `decode_payload` asserts `not isinstance(payload, FilteredPayload)`, so a `FilteredPayload` will raise and be routed through the same log-and-drop/mark-complete path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Error-handling test only passes due to a timing race (commit loop tick vs sleep) and validates nothing about failure handling, rubber-stamping the broken failure semantics

adjudication.rationale: The new queue consumer commits offsets even when processing fails: `OrderedQueueWorker.run` calls `self.offset_tracker.complete_offset(...)` in the `finally` block even after `except Exception`, which makes failed offsets committable and the `_commit_loop` will commit them. The added uptime test `test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling` then asserts no commits occurred, but it can “pass” only because the commit loop sleeps up to 1s (`shutdown_event.wait(1.0)`) and the test breaks as soon as the queues drain + a short `time.sleep(0.2)`, potentially before any commit tick. So the finding about a timing race and the test rubber-stamping broken failure semantics is grounded in the diff and corresponds to a real correctness/data-loss defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.join() re-invokes close(), which sets shutdown_event, joins the commit thread, then drains the queue pool — items completed during drain are never committed, causing duplicate side effects on redelivery; double close/join also re-calls q.shutdown on already-shutdown queues, masking errors

adjudication.rationale: In `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()`, the shutdown sequence is `shutdown_event.set()` then `commit_thread.join(...)` and only afterward `queue_pool.shutdown()` (which stops workers). Worker threads call `offset_tracker.complete_offset(...)` after processing items, but the commit loop (`_commit_loop`) stops as soon as `shutdown_event` is set, so any offsets completed by workers after the commit thread exits will never be committed. That can lead to reprocessing/duplicate side effects on redelivery. This behavior is visible directly in the diff (new `queue_consumer.py`: `close`, `_commit_loop`, and worker `finally:` completing offsets). The finding’s additional claim about “double close/join” is not fully verifiable from the diff alone, but the missed-commit-on-shutdown issue is.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No backpressure despite the docstring claim: queue.Queue is unbounded and submit never blocks, so if processing is slower than consumption memory grows until OOM (no maxsize or bounded poll/pause)

adjudication.rationale: In `FixedQueuePool.__init__` each worker queue is created as `queue.Queue()` with no `maxsize`, making it unbounded. `FixedQueuePool.submit` then calls `work_queue.put(work_item)` without any explicit bounding/pause mechanism, so ingestion will not apply backpressure and can grow memory if processing lags. This contradicts the `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` docstring claim of "Natural backpressure when queues fill up" and can lead to unbounded memory usage/OOM under sustained load.

adjudication_records.issue_text: get_committable_offsets requires contiguous offsets, so messages never seen by strategy.submit (filtering, restart mid-batch) create offset gaps that stall commits forever with no error or metric

adjudication.rationale: In `OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets`, the loop breaks not only on outstanding offsets but also when an offset in the numeric range `[start, max_offset]` is not present in `all_offsets` (`if offset in all_offsets and offset not in outstanding: ... else: break`). This means if the consumer ever observes non-contiguous offsets for a partition (e.g., receives 100 then 102 with 101 never submitted/added), it will commit 100 and then permanently stall at the missing 101 because that offset will never be added to `all_offsets`. The diff does not include any error/metric for this stalled state (only metrics when commits happen), so it can deadlock commits silently. Note: the finding’s example of `FilteredPayload` doesn’t apply because `submit` explicitly adds+completes the offset when `result is None`, but the gap-stall behavior is real given the tracker logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: terminate() never joins the commit thread, so the daemon thread can die mid-commit leaving consumer group state inconsistent with last_committed; close/terminate both call queue_pool.shutdown causing double-shutdown

adjudication.rationale: In `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.__init__` a daemon `commit_thread` is started. `close()` sets `shutdown_event` and then `join()`s the commit thread, but `terminate()` only sets `shutdown_event` and immediately calls `queue_pool.shutdown()` without joining the commit thread. This is verifiable in the diff and can leave the commit thread running concurrently (and it can still execute one loop body after the event is set because the `while not is_set()` check is only at the top), potentially committing offsets after termination or being killed mid-commit at process shutdown due to `daemon=True`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: wait_until_empty's qsize()==0 check ignores in-flight items, and tests gating on total_items==0 as 'processed' can pass before processing completes

adjudication.rationale: In `FixedQueuePool.wait_until_empty`, the condition `self.get_stats()["total_items"] == 0` is based solely on `queue.Queue.qsize()` (via `get_stats`), which only counts items still enqueued, not items already dequeued by a worker and currently being processed. Since `OrderedQueueWorker.run()` calls `work_queue.get()` (removing the item from the queue) before executing `result_processor(...)`, `total_items` can become 0 while work is still in-flight. Therefore `wait_until_empty` can return True prematurely. The same issue applies to tests/polling that treat `stats["total_items"] == 0` as meaning processing is complete (e.g., uptime tests looping on `queue_pool.get_stats()`), which can pass before processing/offset completion has finished.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OffsetTracker.last_committed ignores actual start offsets (initializes at -1 while consumption may resume at 5000); if first seen offset is below the true resume point, commit_offsets' +1 can rewind the consumer group

adjudication.rationale: In `OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets`, the scan starts at `start = max(last_committed + 1, min_offset)`. Even though `last_committed` defaults to `-1`, `min_offset` is derived from the first offsets actually *seen* in `add_offset`, so the tracker will not attempt to commit below the lowest observed offset. The only way to “rewind” a consumer group would be if the consumer delivered messages from offsets lower than the group’s real resume point; that behavior is outside what this diff shows. The diff also does not show any use of the `partitions` start offsets that would contradict the observed offsets. The `+1` adjustment is applied only in `create_thread_queue_parallel_worker` when calling `commit`, consistent with Kafka’s “next offset to read” semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: hash() on str is process-randomized, which would silently break queue-assignment distribution if moving to multiprocessing or persisting assignments

adjudication.rationale: In `FixedQueuePool.get_queue_for_group`, queue selection is `return hash(group_key) % self.num_queues`. Python’s built-in `hash(str)` is salted per process (changes across interpreter runs and between different processes), so group→queue assignment is not stable across restarts and would differ across processes if this approach were ever extended to multiprocessing or if assignments needed to be persisted/shared. In the current diff it’s thread-based within a single process, so it’s not an immediate correctness bug, but it is a real, diff-grounded design concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: WorkItem.message retained per queued item needlessly inflates memory given the offset tracker already carries commit state

adjudication.rationale: In `queue_consumer.py`, `WorkItem` stores `message: Message[...]` and `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit` populates it, but downstream (`OrderedQueueWorker.run`) only uses `work_item.result` and offset tracking uses `partition`/`offset` via `OffsetTracker`. The `message` field is never referenced elsewhere in the diff, so retaining the full `Message`/payload per queued item is unnecessary and can increase memory usage under backlog without improving correctness.
